Share on X Telegram The Upper Area Court sitting in Gudu District, Abuja, has adjourned the divorce case involving Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, and his second wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, till December 15, 2026.
The matter, marked CV/97/26, came up for mention on Tuesday before Justice Ado Mukhtar, following a civil summons directing the governor to appear in court on November 17, 2026.
At the proceedings, the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who received the court processes on behalf of the governor, told the court that he was yet to brief his principal on the development.
Bature, who appeared as the governor’s representative, consequently requested an adjournment to enable him to inform Yusuf and his legal team about the court processes.
Counsel to the petitioner, Aliyu Musa Baba, did not oppose the request.
The presiding judge subsequently adjourned the matter until December 15 for hearing.
Speaking with journalists after the proceedings, Bature said he became aware of the case after hearing reports that a matter involving the governor had been filed before the court.
He explained that he subsequently collected the court processes on behalf of the governor but had yet to brief him on the development.
“Since the court fixed today for mention, I came to inform the court that I had not been able to brief him on the service I collected. He will have to decide on the next course of action,” he said.
Bature said he would exercise restraint in commenting on the matter because it was personal and already before the court.
“This is a personal matter, so I want to exercise some level of restraint because it concerns him personally and is also before the court. We do not want to overflog an issue that is already before the court,” he said.
He also urged journalists to maintain neutrality in reporting the dispute, stressing that it involved a family matter.
“We have to remain very neutral in issues like this because they involve families. Many other stories are newsworthy, rather than focusing on sensational issues like this,” he added.
The development comes a day after Yusuf publicly acknowledged the marital crisis between him and Zainab, a niece of his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.
The governor disclosed this on Monday while addressing pensioners at the Government House in Kano.
Speaking in Hausa, Yusuf likened his marital situation to a demotion in military rank, saying he had moved from being a “corporal” to a “constable” because he now had only one wife.
“Some days ago, I was being forced to become a constable. I want to thank the good people of Kano who advised me to keep two wives, but for now I have accepted one,” he said.
The governor, however, suggested that he might marry again in the future, adding that he had accepted the development.
He also indicated that steps had been taken towards dissolving the marriage, stating that the divorce papers had been issued.
“The governor has agreed to divorce her. The paper for the dissolution has been issued,” he said.
